# UI Framework for Unity

> UI Framework for Unity: smooth, organized game UI, AI-ready. Build Unity game UI from Addressable scenes on a state stack, with shared elements, built-in animations and an editor (UI Setup Manager) that generates the scripts, scenes and config for you. Free and open source (MIT), by Dawaniyah Games. Works with Unity 6 (6000.0 LTS) and newer.

Use it when a Unity game's UI needs a clear structure: every screen gets the same shape (its own Addressable scene, its own script, its own place in the state stack), so code written by a team or by AI coding tools always has a clear place to go. It also gives popups and overlays on top of screens, shared bars that stay on screen, UI that loads on demand, smooth transitions with no empty frame, and merge-friendly files for teams.

## Install

- Unity Package Manager → Add package from git URL: `https://github.com/dawaniyah-games/UiFramework.git?path=Packages/com.dawaniyahgames.uiframework`
- Pin a version by appending `#vX.Y.Z` (latest releases: https://github.com/dawaniyah-games/UiFramework/releases)
- Requirements: Unity 6 (6000.0 LTS) or newer, Addressables 2.2.2+ (installed as a dependency)

## Core API

- `await UiManager.InitializeAsync()` creates the manager and loads `UiConfig` from Addressables.
- `await UiManager.ShowState<T>(context, additive)` shows a state; `additive: true` pushes a popup/overlay on top.
- `await UiManager.HideUI()` pops and unloads the top state.
- `UiElement.Populate(object context)` is the single data contract for every element; keep it idempotent.
- `UiTransition.ShowWith(TweenPresets.ScaleKey)` overrides the animation for one call. Presets: Fade, Scale, SlideUp/Down/Left/Right, ClickPop, SettlePop, Shake.

## Key concepts

- Element: one UI piece (e.g. MainMenuUiElement), one Addressable scene with the contract `<Name>Root → Canvas → Root`.
- State: a list of element scenes shown together (e.g. StoreUiState = TopBar + Store + NavBar). State class names must equal state keys.
- Shared elements: scenes used by consecutive states stay loaded and do not re-animate.
- Reference counting: scenes unload only when no state on the stack uses them.

## Building UI with an AI assistant

- [AI build guide](https://github.com/dawaniyah-games/UiFramework/blob/main/Packages/com.dawaniyahgames.uiframework/Documentation~/ai-builder/SKILL.md): how an assistant should build Unity UI with the framework. Plan screens as element scenes and states, import art from Figma or Photoshop as sprite atlases with ASTC compression, make layouts responsive in the Inspector (anchors, layout groups, aspect fitters; a generic helper component only as the last step), follow the coding standards, and hand off with a checklist.
- [UI_PROFILE.md template](https://github.com/dawaniyah-games/UiFramework/blob/main/Packages/com.dawaniyahgames.uiframework/Documentation~/ai-builder/references/project-profile.md): one file per project with target devices, canvas settings, art pipeline and budgets, so assistants don't ask every time.
